topic: The Impact of Generative AI on Software Developer Productivity and Code Quality
hypothesis: Generative AI tools significantly increase developer productivity for routine coding tasks while maintaining or slightly reducing initial code quality, requiring additional review effort.
competing_hypotheses: Generative AI dramatically increases both productivity and code quality across all software engineering tasks.
Generative AI provides minimal productivity gains after accounting for debugging and review time, and decreases long-term maintainability.
Productivity gains from generative AI are highly sensitive to developer experience level and task complexity.
falsification_criteria: Controlled empirical studies showing no statistically significant productivity difference between developers using generative AI and control groups.
Evidence showing widespread increases in defect rates or vulnerability introduction without offsetting efficiency gains.
Data indicating negative productivity impacts across experienced engineering cohorts.
evaluation_criteria: Developer productivity shall be assessed by task completion time, lines of code per hour, and self-reported efficiency metrics.
Code quality shall be assessed by bug density, code review cycle times, test coverage, and security vulnerability scan results.

evidence_sufficiency.medium: Useful empirical evidence exists from industry reports or limited studies, but sample sizes, metrics, or independent replications are somewhat limited.
evidence_sufficiency.high: Multiple strong independent peer-reviewed studies and empirical evaluations consistently demonstrate measurable productivity and quality outcomes with clear statistical significance.
evidence_sufficiency.conflicting: Comparable empirical studies report contradictory outcomes regarding productivity gains versus code quality degradation.
evidence_sufficiency.low: Evidence is primarily based on anecdotal developer feedback, limited non-peer-reviewed blogs, or highly restricted experimental tasks.
evidence_sufficiency.insufficient: Available evidence lacks rigorous methodology, sufficient sample sizes, or adequate controls to justify any conclusion on productivity or quality impact.
